newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Skanska, IKANO to build outlet stores.
newsitem.headline: Skanska, IKANO to build outlet stores.

text.p: Swedish construction company Skanska AB said on Monday it and IKANO, owned by the family which founded furniture retailer IKEA, would create a company that would specialise in factory outlet stores.
The company, Scandinavian Outlet Parks AB, would set up its first store near Stockholm but planned to expand within Europe, Skanska and IKANO said in a statement.
The first store, which will be Sweden's first factory outlet, will be open in time for Christmas next year, it said.
Other locations for future stores were being researched in the area near the coming bridge link between Denmark and Sweden as well as in Finland, Norway and central Europe, the companies said.

"The potential for factory outlets is big in Europe and in Sweden and we believe that our knowledge in retail sales combined with Skanska's building competence will create synergies," IKANO's Mats Haggblom said in the statement.
The stores would be between 15,000 and 25,000 square metres.

"With IKANO we have a strong partner financially with experience in retail sales the world over. Our combined competence and financial base means we have good potential to expand," said Jan-Erik Hojvall of Skanska Fastigheter.
Hojvall will be mananing director of the new company.
